## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ārāmadūsakajātaka* (Ja 268) is a canonical birth story preserved in the *Jātaka* collection of the Pali Sutta Piṭaka [catalog record]. According to the traditional framing narrative, the Buddha recounted this discourse while staying in the countryside near Dakkhiṇagiri, taking the son of a gardener as the occasion for the instruction.

In the canonical identification of births (*samodhāna*) that concludes the tale, the Buddha reveals that the chief of the monkeys in the past life was reborn as the park-spoiling lad (*ārāmadūsakakumāra*), whereas the wise man (*paṇḍitapurisa*) who observed the scene was the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1879]. In the standard editorial arrangement of the collection, the text directly precedes the *Sujātajātaka* [Fausböll 1879].
